title: cost-optimization-autotune-defaults-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Evelyn Park
release_notes: Automated default tuning for batching/caching and quantization profiles; unit-economics dashboard additions; safe rollout via canary and autoscaling integration.
description: Motivation: running LLM inference at scale requires balancing latency SLOs against per-token cost. This PR automates sensible defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduces model-specific quantization profiles, and ships initial unit-economics (UEcon) tooling to evaluate cost impact across routes. The goal is to reduce median cost-per-request while preserving 99th percentile latency targets and making recommendations actionable in the Console. Changes in this PR: 1) Autotune: new autoscaler hook (autotune service) that analyzes request size distribution and suggests batch_size, enqueue_timeout_ms, and cache_hot_prefix settings. 2) Defaults: safer default batch and cache settings for the most common model families (Llama2, Falcon, Mistral) that bias towards lower latency on interactive traffic and higher batching for long-form generation. 3) Quant profiles: adds quantization presets (int8/4-bit hybrid) per model architecture, with metadata to indicate expected throughput gain and estimated quality regression (QA score ranges from eval harness). 4) UEcon tooling: backend endpoint + Console route to show per-route token cost breakdown, recommended changes, and projected monthly savings if recommendations are applied. 5) Migration and rollout: canary rollout policy and automatic rollback if canary error/latency exceeds thresholds; manifests for Dedicated pools to accept updated defaults. Testing: unit tests for autotune heuristics, integration tests for config propagation to serving runtime, end-to-end perf runs on perf-canary with synthetic traffic (results below). Checklist: - [x] Autotune core algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Default profiles added for 6 common models - [x] Quant profiles annotated with eval metadata - [x] UEcon endpoints implemented and basic Console UI wired - [x] Canary rollout + rollback verified on staging - [x] Docs updated with best-practices and explanation of safety rails Links: Linear ENG-4123 (autotune), perf-canary runs https://internal.redwood/perf/61005. Notes on safety: defaults are conservative and opt-in for Dedicated unless customer enables managed-optimization. For hosted API, recommendations are surfaced and can be applied by Console or via API. Performance summary (perf-canary baseline->post-change): - Median p95 latency change: +6% for interactive 2-token completions on Llama2-medium when applying more aggressive batching, but when using conservative defaults observed no increase. - Throughput on long-form workloads improved by ~18% (effective tokens/sec) with quant profiles enabled and batching tuned. - Estimated per-token cost reduction across sample customers: 9-22% depending on workload mix. Migration plan: gradual rollout by account tier; low-risk canaries for 1% accounts -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring alerts and automated rollback triggers. Backwards compatibility: configs are additive; existing explicit customer overrides remain unchanged. Request for reviewers: please focus on autotune heuristics correctness, security review of new UEcon endpoints, and quant metadata accuracy.

review_comments: Ravi Singh: The autotune heuristics look reasonable but we need a guard against low-traffic churn causing noisy suggestions. Can you add an exponential smoothing window and min-samples threshold?
Evelyn Park: Added smoothing (alpha=0.2) and a default min_samples=200 in the latest commit. Also added unit tests simulating bursty traffic.
Marta Lopez: Quant profiles: can you include the eval-harness job IDs and sample prompt sets used for the QA regressions? We should avoid implying exact numbers without reproducible evals.
Evelyn Park: Included eval-harness IDs in quant_profiles.yaml and linked prompt-set names in the docs. Notes indicate expected variance per dataset.
Noah Kim: UEcon endpoint looks good. Security consideration: ensure only internal service accounts + admin Console can read aggregated recommendations. Confirmed RBAC check added.
Evelyn Park: RBAC check added using existing rbac-policy-bundle rules; unit tests updated to assert access control.
ci_checks: Perf-canary: initial run failed (timeout on synthetic runner), re-run -> pass
perf_results_summary: perf-canary (staging) run on 24-Feb-2026: baseline vs tuned profiles: median tokens/sec +18% on long-form generation (Mistral-7B), p99 latency maintained within 5% for interactive workloads when using conservative defaults. Quant profile int8-hybrid shows 12% cost improvement with <1.5% QA regression on our eval prompt set.
migration_steps: 1) Deploy autotune service to staging; 2) Run perf-canary validation job; 3) Enable recommendations UI flag in Console; 4) Canary apply defaults at 1% of accounts (monitor for 48h); 5) Gradually increase to 10%, 50%, 100% with automated rollback on alerts; 6) Rollout to Dedicated pools as opt-in managed optimization
manual_testing_instructions: Run perf-canary job locally via ./scripts/run_canary --job default-profiles.yml and verify uecon endpoint returns recommendations for sample route 'chat/default' ; inspect console at /console/uecon to see suggested savings; run integration tests in services/autotune/tests to validate smoothing behavior.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge after approvals from Ravi Singh and Marta Lopez. Canary validations green. Backout plan documented in docs/operations/autotune.md.
